350: Poet Laureate is the title given to the poet who receives a stipend as an
officer of the English Royal Household; he is expected to provide poems for
official occasions, such as coronations and weddings. The Poet Laureate at the
time was John Masefield (1878-1967), who had composed "A Prayer for the
King's Reign" (The Times [London), 28 April 1937) to celebrate the accession
of George VI (1895-1952). George became king when his brother Edward
VIII (1894-1972) abdicated to marry Mrs. Wallis Simpson (1896-1986), who
was divorced.
